t: This is Marble Arch, a white marble-faced triumphal arch. John Nash designed it in 1827 as the state entrance to the courtyard of Buckingham Palace, where it stood near the central part of the palace with the famous balcony. Nash was the Georgian and Regency architect behind many important parts of London, with his work financed by the Prince Regent. A different link here is Colonel Edward Douglas Brown-Synge-Hutchinson, an Anglo-Irish soldier who received the Victoria Cross, and who died here.
